title: A House Divided
notebook: Twelve priests in Aldenmoor call the education policy morally indefensible and want Renek to resign.
They cite the government language charter as proof the Church has failed its people.
Vyktor: backing the schismatics loses 400 schools. Backing Renek alienates reformists and Dravenni.
Renek asks whether I will let the Church schism, or help close the wound.

narrative.text: Archbishop Stanislov Renek does not make house calls to the Palace. He sends letters, he summons ministers, he issues pastoral letters. But tonight, he is sitting in your study, his robes heavy with the rain outside, his face pale with a fury he is struggling to contain.

Twelve priests. Twelve men of God in Aldenmoor have stood before their congregations and declared the Church's education policy 'morally indefensible.' They are calling for my resignation. They are citing your government's language charter as proof that the Church has failed the people.

The Dravenni charter. I forced it through to protect minority rights, and now it is tearing the Church apart. Renek is being devoured by his own flock for opposing a policy I implemented. I should feel triumphant. I just broke the Church's political back. Instead, I am looking at an old man who is terrified of losing the only institution he has ever served.
This is your doing, Chancellor. You put the state between me and my priests. Now I am asking you: will you let the Church schism, or will you help me close this wound before it becomes a fracture?
If we back Renek, we alienate the reformists and the Dravenni. If we back the schismatics, the Church collapses, and we lose 400 schools across the Republic overnight.

choices.text: The Church must modernize. I will grant state protection to the reformist priests and seize the schools they administer.
The state does not interfere in Church governance. I will publicly affirm Renek's authority and condemn the schismatics.
Offer to mediate. Set up a council between Renek and the reformists. Keep the state neutral.

narrative.text: You would tear the cloth rather than mend it. So be it. But know this, Chancellor: the Church is the only thing holding this country together in the dark. When you tear it, you will find out what was holding the dark back.
Renek leaves without waiting for an escort. Vyktor watches the door close.
The reformists will cheer. The Dravenni will feel vindicated. But Renek is right about one thing: we just took responsibility for 400 schools, and we don't have the teachers to run them.

choices.text: The state will find the teachers. The dark can be held back by the state, too.

narrative.text: You have chosen wisely, Chancellor. The Church will remember who stood with her in her hour of trial.

I just saved Renek's position and doomed the reformists' hopes. I tell myself it was for stability, for the schools, for the 40,000 Dravenni children who still need a roof. But I know the truth: I chose the power I could negotiate with over the principle I believed in.
A council. You want me to sit at a table with men who called me a tyrant from the pulpit.
But he nods. He knows he has no other leverage. The state's neutrality is the only thing keeping him from a public fall.
A council buys time. It doesn't solve the schism, but it delays the fracture until after the referendum. In politics, a delay is sometimes the only victory you get.

choices.text: Time is the only thing the state has plenty of right now.
